notes: Characters can belong to a family and know where they stand in it. Give everyone in a household the same word in the new Family field and each one is told their own relationship to you, their age, and who every other member is to you — enough for them to work out their own relationship to each other without anyone writing out every pair. A Ties field covers what that cannot reach on its own: whose child is whose, which side a relative is on. They then talk about each other by name, as people who share a life rather than strangers being introduced. Editing anyone's relationship updates what all the others are told immediately. The starter household comes filled in — mother, two sisters, an aunt and a cousin, with the ages and connections between them already set — and characters with no family named are unaffected.
